resolved_in_this_pass.reason: Speaker guidelines grant conditional permission to replay Hansard webcast video for education, private study, research, criticism, review, and newspaper summary; broadcasters may use excerpts for fair and accurate reports.
Parliament web-use rules prohibit reproduction or distribution of portal material without prior express consent and require prior conformity for links.

Congress legal notice allows reuse with attribution/integrity conditions; FAQ says the institutional signal is distributed free to media and citizens and archived videos may be downloaded and used freely after sessions.
General website permissions exist, but audiovisual-material rights questions are directed to Council of Europe audiovisual contacts.
House Broadcasts page is information-purpose only; OpenMB reuse terms were not confirmed to cover legislative audio/video.
Official proceedings page and rules document broadcast access and captions, but not third-party playback or redistribution permission.
Stortinget retransmission terms require a formal arrangement and dedicated publication point; the browser-discovered HLS endpoint is now retained only as evidence and presented as link-out.
Bundestag terms offer a live signal to third parties on request; the browser-discovered HLS endpoint is not that documented route and is now retained only as evidence and presented as link-out.

recommended_next_actions: Send short written-clarification requests for likely_needs_written_clarification entries, starting with Ontario/Nunavut, Netherlands, India, Israel, and Council of Europe/PACE.
Keep keep_pending_after_dated_search entries pending under the prototype policy; revisit during scheduled rights reviews or if source owners publish clearer terms.
If a stricter post-POC policy is adopted, use direct_playback_if_stricter_policy_adopted as the demotion review list.
